problem: No unified scene representation serves both large-scale navigation and fine-grained manipulation. Existing open-vocabulary representations are either offline and per-scene optimized (LERF, ConceptGraphs) or object-level only, so they are too slow or too coarse for real-time mobile manipulation.
motivation: Mobile manipulation needs geometry and language-aligned semantics at both room scale and part scale, in real time on an onboard computer. Generalizable NeRFs trained with novel view synthesis appear to acquire geometric and semantic priors, and could replace per-scene optimization with a single feed-forward pass.
key_idea: Pre-train a scene-level generalizable NeRF encoder on RGB-D novel view synthesis with SDF supervision, and distill CLIP (MaskCLIP) features into it, giving a feed-forward, incremental, language-aligned 3D feature field usable for both navigation and manipulation.
insight: Feed-forward feature fields give online performance that batch methods cannot match, and the continuous representation supports part-level queries where ConceptGraph fails (0-15% vs GeFF 44-80%). The ablation shows that feeding teacher CLIP features as auxiliary encoder input improves generalization to objects unseen in ScanNet (41/66 vs 25/66). The learned geometry prior also compresses well: 512 latent points give a depth L2 error of 0.012, versus 0.040 for bilinear projection.
method: Generalizable NeRF encoder: a trainable encoder on posed RGB-D frames produces a sparse latent point cloud, built incrementally by concatenating per-frame latents; pre-trained via novel view synthesis on ScanNet.

Language alignment via feature distillation: an isotropic g_sem decodes a feature at each 3D point; features are volume-rendered and trained with L2 against MaskCLIP (ViT-L) features of ground-truth novel views.
Auxiliary teacher input: the frozen teacher's 2D features on the input views are concatenated to the encoder's latents (Eq. 3) to improve generalization.
Neural SDF geometry head: g_geo predicts SDF, trained with iSDF-style SDF loss plus Eikonal regularization; opacity is derived from the SDF for depth and feature rendering.

Query handling: cosine similarity with positive and negative text queries under a temperatured softmax; part-level queries use LERF-TOGO conditional CLIP queries and DBSCAN with a small eps (1 cm) on multi-view in-wrist camera observations.

Navigation and manipulation pipeline: decode a point cloud and a 2D semantic grid map; use DBSCAN for goals, an affordance-aware A* planner for navigation, and an OMPL sample-based planner with an open-push-close gripper sequence for grasping.

setting.backbone: GeFF generalizable NeRF encoder (trained), with frozen MaskCLIP ViT-L as the distillation teacher
setting.training_data: ScanNet (RGB-D novel view synthesis plus CLIP feature distillation), 50 epochs on 8 RTX3090 GPUs for 6 days
setting.observation: Posed RGB-D stream (stereo and structured-light cameras on the head, plus an in-wrist camera), with poses from HybVIO
setting.action_space: 2D navigation with an affordance-aware A* planner over a grid map; arm motion planned with OMPL; open-push-close gripper actions
setting.privileged: none (the initial scene scan is driven manually, and receptacle/object names are given by the user)

numbers.extra: Unitree B1 + Z1 arm; onboard AGX Orin; latency 0.39s; 4 real environments, 17 objects at object level; part-level: 3 categories x 4 instances

results: GeFF achieves 62.4% overall success (average of object-level and part-level manipulation), at 0.39s latency on the onboard AGX Orin. This beats LERF (43.2%, about 2 hrs offline) and ConceptGraph (41.9%, about 200s offline), and the online ConceptGraph variant reaches only 5.3%. ConceptGraph is slightly better at object-level mobile manipulation (72.2% vs 61.1%) but nearly fails at part-level queries.
limitations: MaskCLIP features are coarse, and the encoder was trained only on ScanNet, so the auxiliary CLIP input is needed as a shortcut for generalization.
Manipulation performance is modest (61.1% object-level, 44.4% mug-handle); performance drops under scene change with a single front view.
The initial scene scan is driven manually, and evaluation is small-scale real-world (a few environments, few trials), with no standard benchmarks.
builds_on: Generalizable NeRF scene priors (Yang Fu et al. 2023)
